on 10 January, 2025
Author: Chandra Shekhar Jha

Bench: Chandra Shekhar Jha
 In The High Court Of Judicature At Patna

 Arising Out of Ps. Case No.-340 Year-2022 Thana- Sahpur District

Respondent/s

======================================================
 Appearance :
 For the Appellant/s : Mr. Sachin Kumar, Adv.
 For the Respondent/s : Mr. Sadanand Paswan, Spl.PP  ======================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE CHANDRA SHEKHAR JHA  ORAL ORDER 4 10-01-2025 1.
Heard the parties.

2. The appellant has preferred the present appeal under Section 14A(2) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (hereinafter referred to as the "SC/ST Act")
against the refusal of prayer for bail vide order dated 25.07.2024 passed by the learned Exclusive Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Civil court (Sadar), Patna, in connection with Shahpur P.S. Case No. 340 of 2022 registered for the offences under Sections 406, 420, 467, 468/34 of the Patna High Court CR.

4. Notice appears served to respondent no. 2 by way of substituted mode of service, which shows that it has been served validly upon informant but failed to join the present proceedings.

sentences.text: Allegation against the appellant is to cheat Rs. 11,16,000/- along with named co-accused person on pretext of giving a flat to informant but same was not delivered as promised.
Appellant is said to be Assistant General Manager of the company namely, Patligram Builders Private Limited.

6. It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that the thrust of allegation was against the director of the company namely, Prabhat Kumar Ranjan @ Uday Samrat @ Udai Samrat and Priya Kumari @ Priya Mishra.

entities.text: Prabhat Kumar Ranjan @ Uday Samrat @ Udai Samrat
entities.label: OTHER_PERSON

sentences.text: It is pointed out that co-accused namely, Prabhat Kumar Ranjan @ Uday Samrat @ Udai Samrat Patna High Court CR.

entities.text: Prabhat Kumar Ranjan @ Uday Samrat @ Udai Samrat Patna High Court
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: APP (SJ) No.4354 of 2024(4) dt.10-01-2025 has already granted bail by this Court, considering the compromise arrived between the parties.
It is submitted that appellant was the employee and only explained the project to the informant in terms of FIR.

It is also submitted that one co-accused namely, Brajesh Gandhi also granted anticipatory bail through Cr. APP (SJ) No. 2568 of 2023 dated 13.05.2024.
7.
Learned Spl.PP objected the prayer of bail of the bail of the appellant.

8. Considering the submission as the main accused already granted bail by one of the learned Co- ordinate Bench of this Court on the basis of compromise arrived between the parties, where admittedly appellant was the employee, accordingly, above named appellant, in the event of his arrest or surrender before the learned trial Court, within a period of six weeks of the order, is directed to be released on bail furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Patna High Court CR.
